The Arab kings. {OCR?}
During the days of the fast of the Forty Days,
Mar Denha, the Catholicus of the Nestorians, seized a man of Tikrit who had become a Muslim {lit. Hagarene} for a long time,
and intended to drown him in the Tigris.
And the common people {or Muslims} of Baghdad heard [of it],
and made a great riot against ‘Ala al-Din, the Sahib al-Diwan.
And he sent to the Catholicus several times [through] noble men,
and demanded that individual from him.
And when he was unwilling to give [him] up,
the common people became infuriated,
and set fire to the porticoes of the doors of the cell {or residence},
and climbed up the walls to kill the Catholicus.
And the Sahib al-Diwan heard,
and sent and took him to his court secretly from the water side,
and rescued him.
And the Catholicus sent and complained at the Ordu {royal camp},
and emissaries came and took him, and he went.
And when he complained,
no one listened to his voice.
And leaving, he came to Arbela,
and began to build a church in its fortress,
and remained in it.
Concerning the capture of Antioch.
And in June of this year,
Bunduqdar, the ruler of Egypt, sent forces against Antioch, the capital {lit. great city} of Syria,
and they took it by the sword,
because there was not in it a force sufficient for its defense,
nor did those who were in it have the sense to surrender it peacefully.
For this reason the Egyptians entered it,
and killed all its men,
and destroyed its famous churches {or walls?},
and took captive the women and sons and daughters,
and left it desolate and ruined unto this day.
And in the summer of this year, the holy Mar, that Hananisho‘, bishop of the Island {Jazirat Ibn ‘Umar}, was seized,
and the command went forth that he should be killed.
And they killed him, not with the sword,
but while he was reclining {or sleeping} on a couch {OCR?},
they suspended a great stone and struck him on his head from behind him and killed him.
And they cut off his head,
and hung it above the gate of the city of the Island {Jazirah}.
And this evil end befell him,
because he involved himself in worldly affairs,
and desired to become a king,
and he was further accused of shameful fornications.
And at that time, the Egyptian [ruler] sent the worthy {lit. possessor of reward} Lord Leo, son of King Hethum, to his father with honor,
and he entered Cilicia in the month of Tammuz of this year,
and there was comfort to his father and to all the Christians.
And King Hethum went to Baghdad to do homage to the King of Kings,
and offered thanks for the deliverance of his son.
